+1 — experiencing the same issue with `opencode serve` v1.2.24 running behind an auth reverse proxy (HTTP/2 → HTTP/1.1 on localhost:4096).

## Environment

- 12 active workspaces (worktrees/sandboxes)
- ~20 internal TCP connections from the proxy to port 4096
- Linux, 125GB RAM

## Observations

- RSS grows at **~80MB/min** steadily, reaching 24GB+ after <2h
- `smaps_rollup` shows 23.3GB of `Pss_Anon` (pure anonymous heap), all `Private_Dirty`
- TUI mode does **not** exhibit the leak — only `serve` mode
- The leak occurs even when connecting directly via SSH port-forward (bypassing the proxy), confirming it's in `opencode serve` itself
- TCP socket analysis shows `rwnd_limited:100%` on 17/20 internal connections — `opencode serve` is writing data faster than the proxy can drain it, causing send-queue buildup of ~37MB

## Root Cause Analysis

Traced through the source at v1.2.24 (`c6262f9d4`). The primary leak is in the SSE endpoints:

1. **`server.ts:534-560`** — `Bus.subscribeAll()` + `setInterval(heartbeat, 10s)` cleanup is gated entirely on `stream.onAbort()`. When a reverse proxy holds TCP connections open (standard behavior), `onAbort` never fires. The subscription and interval live forever, writing into a `ReadableStream` queue that grows without bound.

2. **`routes/global.ts:85-106`** — same pattern with `GlobalBus.on("event", handler)`. Since `GlobalBus` receives events from all 12 instances, this is the most active leak site.

3. **`bus/index.ts:52-63`** — `Bus.publish()` does `Promise.all(pending)` over all subscribers including stale async SSE callbacks. If a dead stream's `writeSSE()` stalls on backpressure, the entire event pipeline stalls.

4. **`session/index.ts:764`** — `structuredClone(part)` on every LLM token update sends the full accumulated text to all stale subscribers, creating quadratic allocation.

5. **`share/share-next.ts:22-65`** — 4 `Bus.subscribe()` calls per instance with return values discarded. In `serve` mode, `Instance.disposeAll()` is never called, so these subscriptions accumulate forever.

## Checked v1.2.27 (dev HEAD)

The SSE endpoints were partially refactored — `AsyncQueue` now decouples bus events from stream writes (fixing the `Bus.publish` stalling), and a `finally { stop() }` block provides a secondary cleanup path. However, the fundamental issue of cleanup being gated on `stream.onAbort()` persists. If `writeSSE()` buffers without throwing, the `AsyncQueue` grows without bound. The `structuredClone(part)` and `ShareNext` subscription leaks are also still present.

## Suggested Fix

Use `c.req.raw.signal` (`AbortSignal`) as a secondary cleanup trigger. Bun populates this signal when the underlying connection closes, even when `stream.onAbort()` doesn't fire:

```typescript
c.req.raw.signal.addEventListener("abort", stop)
```

This single line added to each SSE endpoint would cover the proxy disconnect case.

I did this for my own use first — it works but it's inherently fragile since we're impersonating Claude Code. OpenCode won't maintain Anthropic OAuth compatibility (PR #18186 made that clear), so this is community-maintained and on borrowed time.

TL;DR of what changed server-side and why most fixes break:
- OAuth endpoints moved from `console.anthropic.com` → `platform.claude.com`
- Anthropic now requires a billing header (SHA-256 based) injected into the request body
- User-Agent `claude-code/*` on API calls gets you rate-limited, `axios/1.13.6` on token exchange doesn't

All of this was reverse-engineered from the Claude Code v2.1.80 binary + MITM traffic analysis. Tests with verified vectors included in the PR.

**Heads up for people using token sync approaches** like [opencode-claude-auth-sync](https://github.com/lehdqlsl/opencode-claude-auth-sync): now that PR #18186 landed, just copying tokens into `auth.json` won't cut it anymore. The tokens are fine, but without the plugin doing billing header injection + correct User-Agent + endpoint rewriting, you'll keep hitting 429s.

If you want to test now before the PR gets merged:
```json
{
  "plugin": ["github:Thesam1798/opencode-anthropic-auth#fix/claude-code-oauth-compatibility"]
}
```

**Note:** you need an OpenCode version **newer than** [PR #18186](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/18186) (merged Mar 19) — older versions still bundle the old `opencode-anthropic-auth@0.0.13` which conflicts. Dev builds `>= 0.0.0-dev-202603200536` or any future stable `>= 1.3.0` should work.

@rurza A few things to check:

1. **Which auth option are you selecting?** When you run `/connect` → Anthropic, you should see **"Claude Pro/Max"** as an option — that's our plugin. If you're selecting a different option (like "Manually enter API Key" or a built-in OAuth), that's OpenCode's own flow, not ours.

2. **"Invalid code" is not our error message** — our plugin shows "Failed to authorize" on failure. If you see "Invalid code", that's likely OpenCode's built-in auth intercepting.

3. **Check your plugin list** — make sure `opencode-anthropic-oauth` is loaded:
   ```
   opencode --print-logs 2>&1 | grep anthropic-oauth
   ```

4. **Remove any conflicting plugins** — if you still have `opencode-anthropic-auth` or `opencode-claude-auth` in your `opencode.json`, remove them. They can conflict.

5. **OpenCode version** — which version are you on? (`opencode --version`)

> Ye guys can, as a workaround, just auth using Claude Code and then have a little script that copies over the tokens from `~/.claude/.credentials.json` to `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json` (need to transform a little though, different formats - or just copy the 2 tokens and the expires manually).

One step further: just generate `auth.json` from `credentials.json` before launch instead of copying fields manually.

E.g. 
```shell
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

AUTH_SRC="${HOME}/.claude/.credentials.json"
AUTH_DST="${HOME}/.local/share/opencode/auth.json"

echo "[INFO] Generating auth.json from Claude credentials..."

command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "[ERROR] jq not installed"; exit 1; }
[[ -f "$AUTH_SRC" ]] || { echo "[ERROR] Missing source file: $AUTH_SRC"; exit 1; }

mkdir -p "$(dirname "$AUTH_DST")"

jq '{
  anthropic: {
    type: "oauth",
    refresh: (.claudeAiOauth.refreshToken // error("missing refreshToken")),
    access: (.claudeAiOauth.accessToken // error("missing accessToken")),
    expires: (.claudeAiOauth.expiresAt // error("missing expiresAt"))
  }
}' "$AUTH_SRC" > "${AUTH_DST}.tmp"

echo "[INFO] Moving generated file into place..."
mv -v "${AUTH_DST}.tmp" "$AUTH_DST"

echo "[INFO] Done."
exec opencode "$@"
```

@tgallacher The plugin needs to be installed globally **and** added to your config. Two steps:

1. Install:
```bash
npm install -g opencode-anthropic-oauth
```

2. Add to your `opencode.json` (usually `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`):
```json
{
  "plugin": ["opencode-anthropic-oauth"]
}
```

Then restart OpenCode. You should see it in the logs:
```bash
opencode --print-logs 2>&1 | grep plugin
```

If it still doesn't show, check where your config file is — it might be in a project-level `opencode.json` instead of the global one.

> 
> echo "[INFO] Generating auth.json from Claude credentials..."
> 
> command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "[ERROR] jq not installed"; exit 1; }
> [[ -f "$AUTH_SRC" ]] || { echo "[ERROR] Missing source file: $AUTH_SRC"; exit 1; }
> 
> mkdir -p "$(dirname "$AUTH_DST")"
> 
> jq '{

>     refresh: (.claudeAiOauth.refreshToken // error("missing refreshToken")),

>     expires: (.claudeAiOauth.expiresAt // error("missing expiresAt"))
>   }
> }' "$AUTH_SRC" > "${AUTH_DST}.tmp"
> 
> echo "[INFO] Moving generated file into place..."

> 
> echo "[INFO] Done."
